about: What a recipe's `wakes` list may say, copied from what the engine's wake primitive accepts, so a recipe that passes here is a wake the engine takes. The engine reads `wakes` from every Workshop row, a listed recipe row included, and a Workshop row's wake is off until the person switches it on; one malformed item refuses every row's wakes, which is why each is checked here before it ships. A wake is { id, on: { <one cause>: { ...its fields } }, budget: { <dimension>: whole number }, input: { start_at: <step id>, ...input_schema fields } }: exactly the engine's declaration, nothing added, and the optional settings of `settings` (retry, skip_unchanged, rate, replay), each refused on a cause its `only_on` does not name. `start_at` in its input is the step a woken run starts at. Adding a cause is adding a row to `causes` once the engine takes it; a field shape is one of text (a non-empty string), texts (a non-empty list of non-empty strings), zone (an IANA time zone name the time zone database knows; a repeat in a zone keeps its wall-clock time), whole (a whole number from 0), positive (a whole number above 0), strings (an object whose values are strings), flag (true or false) or object (any object, kept as written). A cause's `draws` names the ledger its budget comes from, or {by, ledgers, otherwise}: the ledger each value of field `by` names (for a fact, who told it), else `otherwise`; a wake's budget must fit every ledger its values may draw from. A field may carry its own `refusal` words. A field's `in` names a list in this file its value (each item of a texts value) must be one of; `keys_in` names an object in this file whose entry under the value of field `by` lists the keys allowed; `only_with` names a field that must be present for this one to be; `at_least` names a field this one may not be below; `at_most` names a number in this file this one may not be above. The budget must hold at least `least_budget` (the engine's run cost plus its reserved run time, below which a firing is never funded) and at most the ledger its cause draws from (a firing above it is never funded either).

read_from: src/wake.rs: enum On (running, fact; deny_unknown_fields; the engine keeps no clock, so a time comes as a due-time fact a run tells) and Waker::declared (fact kind and from non-empty, from naming the tellers computer, run and sender (COMPUTER, RUN, SENDER), match fields equal to the fact's payload, fold true or false, watch kept as written and never read; budget keys only ledger dimensions, input an object, ids unique per row)

src/wake.rs: Declaration's settings (Retry: attempts at least 1, factor at least 1, most_ms at least first_ms; Unchanged: true or a non-empty list of distinct names; Rate: most and per_ms at least 1; Replay: within_ms at least 1), each only on a fact wake (trillion-rust 07e8dc0c6, c4379950f, 709fb4d34, 71ac34c80); bounds (896150e0d): retry first_ms and most_ms and rate per_ms at most period_ms (most_wait_ms here, wake.json period_ms), rate most at most max_live; replay within_ms 0 owes nothing; needs_input (336aa935c) on any wake
src/wake/wake.json: draws (a fact by its teller, draws.facts run: work, else arrival: inbound)
src/wake/workshop_runner.rs: WAKES_FIELD, the row field the engine reads wakes from
product/wake.json: ledgers, draws, run_cost, wall_dimension, max_wakes
product/tool-runs.json: deadline_ms (the time reserved for every run)

settings.meaning: A run that failed runs again later, as a new cause paid from what the failed run left (never from a ledger, so attempts end at budget zero). attempts counts the first run; attempt 2 waits first_ms, each later one factor (default 2) times longer, at most most_ms. A run whose outcome is unknown is never run again. On a running wake it is how often a start that failed (no session made) is started again; the engine gives running wakes one by default (src/wake/wake.json defaults.running).
A fact whose content is the content of the last fact this wake took starts nothing: true compares the kind and whole payload, a list of payload field names compares the kind and those fields only.
At most `most` causes of this wake become due in any per_ms; a fact over the rate is delayed, never dropped.

The input paths (dot-separated) a switch on must leave this wake's runs holding, from the recipe's own input, the switch's input, or the input the same party gave its last switch on (which a switch on with no input keeps). A switch that would leave one empty is refused, so a wake never runs on without what it needs. Any cause.

A fact this wake heard and could not fund (its ledger or the engine's live cap) is owed to it and taken on a later pass, oldest first, until within_ms after it was told; let go, and counted on the wake's mark as owed_let_go, when the wake is switched off or the window passes. The engine gives every fact wake replay for one period when its row names none (src/wake/wake.json defaults); within_ms 0 owes nothing.

causes.meaning: Keep the tool's program running while the wake is on: one cause starts it as a kept-open session, and switching the wake off ends it.

A fact of this kind, told by one of the tellers in from (computer: the computer the engine runs on; run: one of the person's tool runs, such as the noticer's due times; sender: anyone else at the door; wake: the engine, telling the wake-failed fact it keeps when a wake turns failed; door: the person's door, telling the tool-ran fact once per tool, state and day for a call of their own), whose payload equals every field of match. fold folds a burst into the cause not yet started. watch is what the wake asks a teller to watch for, in the teller's own DATA (for due-time, timed-action schedule rows); the engine keeps it with the wake and lists it.
